title: Fourier omission under an influence bound
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be $\pm1$-valued, let $J\subseteq[n]$, and let $k\in\mathbb N$ and $\rho,\tau\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0\le\rho\le1$ and $\tau\ge0$. If every coordinate $i\notin J$ has influence at most $\tau$, then $\rho^k\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq[n]\\|S|\le k,\ S\nsubseteq J}}\widehat f(S)^2\le\tau^{(1-\rho)/(1+\rho)} I[f]$, where $I[f]$ is the total influence of $f$.
hypotheses_covered: Every coordinate outside $J$ has influence at most $\tau$
replaced: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube, $J\subseteq[n]$, $k\in\mathbb N$, $0\le\rho\le1$, and $\tau\ge0$. If $I_i(f)\le\tau$ for every $i\notin J$, then $\rho^k\sum_{|S|\le k,\ S\nsubseteq J}\widehat f(S)^2\le\tau^{(1-\rho)/(1+\rho)}I(f)$, with $0^0=1$. For a real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation, and $I(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(h)$.
